state.title: Why types beat guesswork
state.metaDescription: A working note on checking claims before publishing them.
state.author: Ada Example
state.text: Ada Example writes on Example Notes that a typed check of a claim is more useful than a generated paragraph. She links the checklist she ran and the numbers from her own run, and she marks the rest as her opinion.

legend.0: Established factual claims are made with little or no supporting evidence, data, or sources on the page.
legend.1: Some established claims have sources or data, or the writing is a proposal or hypothesis whose main particulars are not checkable; important established claims or measurements are still missing.
legend.2: The main factual claims presented as established are backed by named sources, data, documents, or the author's inspectable work.
